scope_contract.goal_statement: To report the existence of an emergency condition that requires search and rescue efforts.
scope_contract.canonical_success_scenario: The System Operator initiates an Emergency Point Report to report the existence of an emergency condition that requires search and rescue efforts.
scope_contract.start_boundary: The System Operator begins initiating an Emergency Point Report.
scope_contract.success_boundary: The System Operator has completed initiating the Emergency Point Report.
in_scope_actions: Reporting the existence of an emergency condition that requires search and rescue efforts
excluded_adjacent_actions: Reporting additional or more current information on a previously reported emergency point
Carrying out search and rescue efforts
Any downstream processing of the initiated report

claims.content: System Operator
The System Operator must have information about an emergency condition that requires search and rescue efforts.
The System Operator initiates an Emergency Point Report through operator action only.

The System Operator, as a JU with R², initiates an emergency alert on a track by setting the appropriate EMG IND in the J3.2 Air Track, J3.3 Surface (Maritime) Track, J3.4 Subsurface (Maritime) Track, or J3.5 Land (Ground) Point/Track message.
The emergency point is transmitted as a J3.1 message.
All receiving JUs accept the alert in their databases upon receipt of the initiation message.
Diverges from Step 3: If the Emergency Point Report is transmitted as a J3.1 message with the Exercise Indicator set to value 1, the report is for exercise purposes and is not an actual emergency.

Diverges from main_flow Step 1: If the System Operator attempts to initiate an Emergency Point Report on a Reference Point or a Space/Ballistic Missile Track, the Emergency Point Report shall not be initiated.
Diverges from main_flow Step 2: If the System Operator attempts to initiate an emergency alert on a Reference Point, Line, or Area, the emergency alert is not used.
Diverges from main_flow Step 3: When the emergency point is transmitted as a J3.1 message, alerts are not used for the J3.1 Emergency Point message because emergency points cannot be filtered.

missing_aspects: Explicit exit or termination condition for the use case.
Explicit instruction to return to a specific main flow step.

claims.content: The Emergency Point Report has been transmitted as a J3.1 message.
All receiving JUs have accepted the emergency alert in their databases.
The reported emergency point has been assigned a TN(s) by the reporting JU, and its position has been reported using geodetic latitude/longitude values.
The System Operator has R² for the emergency point.

missing_aspects: Evidence does not explicitly state that acceptance occurs 'upon receipt of the initiation message'; it states JUs shall accept the alert (initiation) and clear the alert upon receipt of a specific termination/clearing message.

Source evidence defines the rule for 'the latest JU to report a point' having R², but does not identify the actor as the 'System Operator' nor confirm they are the latest reporter in this specific context.
